sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-Myc immunofluorescence in mouse photoreceptors in vivo (L5). Receptor participates in heteromer studies (BRET) but function of the Myc-tagged construct alone was not isolated. NOT MEASURED for isolated functional assay of the tagged receptor.
sites.rationale: MTNR1B is a GPCR with no endogenous signal peptide; the N-terminus (residues 1–42, EC1) is extracellular and the sole extracellular terminus. A tag prepended before residue 1 (insert_after_residue=0, residue_after=M) is therefore the unique surface-accessible terminus, 42 residues from TM1 (residues 43–63), well beyond the ≥3-residue TM-boundary constraint. The 'Myc-MT2' naming convention unambiguously places the Myc tag at the N-terminus; no residue number is given in the paper, so position is topology-derived. Four independent ledger lines (L1–L5) all converge on this same junction with FLAG or Myc tags, providing strong convergent support. Myc-MT2 wild-type receptor expressed as a full-length construct in mouse photoreceptors via lentiviral transduction under the rhodopsin promoter (PMC3867265). Anti-Myc immunofluorescence detected the tagged receptor specifically in photoreceptors (L5, same paper), confirming surface accessibility of the tag. Independently corroborated by FLAG-MTNR1B in HEK293T (L3, PMC12158745) and FLAG-tagged full-length MT2 in baculovirus Sf9 cells (L1, PMC8786939; L2, PMC6589158).

sources.claim: To test whether MT 1 and MT 2 receptors form functional heteromers in the mouse photoreceptors, we developed a series of transgenic mice by transducing mouse fertilized eggs with lentiviral vectors containing Flag-MT 1 or Myc-MT 2 wild-type receptor coding regions under the control of the rhodopsin promoter to drive expression of these receptors in photoreceptor cells.

literature_notes: All five ledger lines (L1–L5) converge on a single junction: the extracellular N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue=0). L1 (PMC8786939) and L2 (PMC6589158) use an exogenous HA signal peptide followed by FLAG on full-length MT2 in baculovirus; after HA-SP cleavage the FLAG sits at the mature N-terminus, the same junction. L3 (PMC12158745) uses FLAG directly at the N-terminus of MTNR1B in HEK293T. L4/L5 (PMC3867265) use Myc-MT2 with surface IF confirmation. Because all lines pin the identical junction (N-terminal prepend), this is reported as one site. The C-terminal His6/10xHis tags in L1 and L2 are intracellular (IC4: residues 309–362) and are recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports any internal extracellular loop insertion for MTNR1B.

literature_other_positions.note: Hexa-histidine tag at the C-terminus of full-length MTNR1B; the C-terminus falls in IC4 (residues 309–362, intracellular) and is not surface-accessible.
10×His tag at the C-terminus of the MT2-CC full-length crystallization construct; same intracellular IC4 location, not a surface tag site.
